As such, linked lists in DSA have the following characteristics: 1.Insertion is O(1) 2.Deletion is O(n) 3.Searching is O(n) Out of the three operations the one that stands out is that of insertion. In DSA we chose to always maintain pointers (or more aptly references) to the node(s) at the head and tail of the linked list and so performing a traditional insertion to either the front or back of the linked list is an O(1) operation. An exception to this rule is performing an insertion before a node that is neither the head nor tail in a singly linked list.
